summary: H.R. 5172, titled the "Strong Sentences for Safer D.C. Streets Act of 2025," establishes and increases mandatory minimum prison sentences for specified crimes committed in the District of Columbia. The changes apply to criminal conduct occurring after the date of enactment.

affected_groups.effect: Face longer mandatory minimum prison sentences, mandatory life imprisonment without release for first-degree murder (including individuals under the age of 18), and higher minimums for repeat violent offenders.
affected_groups.group: Individuals convicted of specified violent crimes in the District of Columbia

key_provisions: Mandates life imprisonment without release for first-degree murder and repeals provisions prohibiting life sentences without parole for individuals under 18 convicted of first-degree murder.
Establishes a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years imprisonment for second-degree murder.
Establishes a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years imprisonment for kidnapping.
Establishes a mandatory minimum sentence of 25 years imprisonment for first-degree sexual abuse.
Increases the mandatory minimum sentence for rape to 25 years imprisonment, and to 30 years if the offender has a prior conviction for a crime of violence.
Increases the mandatory minimum sentence for first-degree burglary from 5 years to 10 years imprisonment.
Increases mandatory minimum sentences for carjacking from 7 years to 10 years for unarmed offenses, and from 15 years to 20 years for armed offenses.

summary_detail.significance: The bill alters sentencing laws in the District of Columbia by removing discretion for certain violent crimes through higher mandatory minimum prison terms and life imprisonment requirements without parole, including for minors convicted of first-degree murder.
